messages:
Sam (Support): Hey team — ACME (customer) reporting sudden p95/p99 regressions starting ~03:45 UTC. They see many requests stuck in our ingress admit queue and timeouts. Repro: curl against /v1/gen with their tenant header. Screenshot attached (500+ms -> 4s p99).
Maya (Eng-Oncall): thanks, Sam. Can you drop the curl + headers and a couple of request IDs? Also which region/cluster?
Sam (Support): Region: eu-west-1. Example request id: req_2026-03-17_03:47:22_axa1. Repro curl: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' -H 'X-Tenant: acme' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/gen -v
Devon (Eng-Runtime): grabbing logs for req_2026-03-17_03:4722_axa1 from ingress. Initial glance shows long queue wait (admit latency ~2.7s) before worker assign. Worker pods at ~98% GPU util; queue length spikes at the same time.
Ivy (Eng-SRE): any autoscaler events or rollout around that time?
Devon (Eng-Runtime): No deploys. Autoscaler shows scale-up attempts but min replicas hit cap for dedicated pool. Also admission controller rejected a batch of extra workers due to tenancy quota.
Maya (Eng-Oncall): hypothesis: sustained burst from a few noisy API keys causing worker pool saturation -> admission backlog. Immediate mitigation options: 1) Temporarily raise concurrency cap for acme on eu-west-1 (if safe) 2) Reroute their traffic to dedicated spare capacity in eu-central 3) Enable fast-fail policy for requests that would exceed queue threshold. Which do we prefer for a hotfix?
Sam (Support): Customer wants quick fix; they allow brief redirection. Reroute sounds best.
Ivy (Eng-SRE): I'll create a temporary routing rule to send X-Tenant: acme to fallback pool (dedicated-spare-1). Pushing now.
deploy-bot: routing-change request created by ivy.sre, id=rout-4991010101-1.
Ivy (Eng-SRE): applied rule. Monitoring now.
Devon (Eng-Runtime): after reroute, ingress admit queue for eu-west-1 for acme dropped from ~120 -> ~5. p95 latency improved from 1.4s -> 180ms, p99 down from 4.2s -> 420ms. CPU/GPU on fallback pool at 60% now.
Sam (Support): told customer we redirected a subset of traffic to a spare pool; they confirmed lower latency for their test requests. :thumbsup:
Maya (Eng-Oncall): good. Next: root cause actions — we need to block noisy keys (rate-limit), increase tenant burst quota safeguards, and ensure autoscaler can borrow from burst capacity instead of hitting quota hard. Also add an alert for admit-queue-length > 50 sustained for 5m.
Devon (Eng-Runtime): I'll open runtime ticket to add a soft quota-borrow fallback and improve admission backoff metrics. Ticket ENG-RUNTIME-642.
Ivy (Eng-SRE): I'll adjust runbook: add explicit reroute step and checklist to confirm quota headroom before scaling. Also will create the admit-queue alert.
Sam (Support): Customer asks about why this started now — they had a release that increased parallel calls per session. We'll advise usage patterns and push recommended throttles in docs.
Maya (Eng-Oncall): temporary measures deployed -> leaving reroute in place for 30m while we monitor; plan follow-ups: (a) out-of-band meeting with ACME to review rate patterns, (b) implement tenant-level burst protect in 48h, (c) postmortem doc.
Devon (Eng-Runtime): quick diagnostic snippets for postmortem:
```
# check admit queue length
kubectl -n ingress logs ingress-controller | grep admit_queue | tail -n 50
# sample worker GPU util
kubectl -n runtime top pods | grep worker | sort -rk3 | head
```
Maya (Eng-Oncall): thanks. Closing immediate escalation — will convert to incident follow-up and attach logs. Sam, please flag customer comms and ETA.
Sam (Support): Will update ACME with summary + ETA for permanent fixes. Leaving thread open for postmortem notes.
Ivy (Eng-SRE): saved monitoring snapshot and created incident INC-4991010101.
Devon (Eng-Runtime): created runtime ticket ENG-RUNTIME-642 and linked to incident.
Sam (Support): marking customer satisfied for now. Will post final summary here in 24h.
Maya (Eng-Oncall): good work team. :rocket:
